findings.issue: The 'rounds half up' cases (1/3 -> 33.3, 1/8 -> 12.5, 1/1500 -> 0.1) never hit an exact x.x5 tenths boundary, so a half-down or banker's rounding rate would still pass. It is low risk because rateTiles reuses bbPer100, which already has half-up tests, and the spec's own examples are covered exactly.
findings.evidence: expect(rates(8, 1)).toEqual(['8', '12.5', '0.0']); 1/8*100 = 12.5 exactly, so no rounding happens at one decimal.

summary: The change matches the spec. Errors counts skip hinted decisions in both rates. Forced folds have no decision entry, so they can't count, and SPEC-05 covers that. errors is present only when there is at least 1 hand and every hand has decisions (SPEC-07 tests no hands, [], mixed, and all-empty). Rates come from bbPer100(count,1,handsPlayed).toFixed(1) and never show -0. parseErrors enforces whole numbers from 0 to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and the null/[]/-1/1.5/'2'/missing cases are tested for both fields. The three locked TASK-10.4 tests match their state.json hashes, and the diff touches no earlier locked tests. reportView, hand-store and advice are unchanged. All gates pass (fix-2). The SPEC-04 120 s timeout and the getByLabel locator are reasonable recorded deviations. Only a MINOR type cast and a NIT about rounding-test coverage were found.
